source.title: Criticality versus uniformity in deep neural networks
source.authors: A. Bukva; Jurriaan de Gier; Kevin T. Grosvenor; R. Jefferson; K. Schalm; Eliot Schwander

record.tranche_reason: Tests how initialization variances and activation saturation affect learning accuracy, using a different setup and measure from the versions’ stated benchmarks and training-error claims.
record.gate_note: The paper reports accuracy outcomes for its own initialization and saturation experiments. Prior-work results cited in the paper are not extracted. Several plotted outcomes lack exact numerical values in the text; those rows are marked figure only.
record.test_reason: The study tests V4 through its own Gaussian-initialization sweeps and accuracy after fixed training budgets in plain tanh networks. It reproduces the advantage of critical initialization for trainable depth and tests whether criticality alone ensures efficient learning.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors find that tanh saturation can impair fixed-budget SGD learning even at critical initialization. The line of uniformity gives a rough indication of this deterioration, rather than a sharp boundary; its location depends on learning rate and dataset. They interpret criticality as necessary but insufficient for optimal trainability, without establishing that fixed-budget accuracy differences persist indefinitely.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies random feedforward networks with Gaussian weight and bias initialization, sweeping variance settings and measuring accuracy; it does not reproduce the recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy varies with initial weight and bias variances, activation saturation, learning rate, dataset, network width and depth. The location and sharpness of the accuracy drop-off depend on learning rate and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: The 40-layer SWISH network shows no significant accuracy differences across the computable critical initialization range, with smaller learning rates at two points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fixed-budget SWISH accuracy remains approximately unchanged across the tested edge-of-chaos range.

record.problems: The main findings are primarily shown in figures without exact accuracy values in the supplied text. The small-network uniformity analysis applies large-N reasoning to N = 8 and reports order-one discrepancies from analytical predictions. Accuracy is not explicitly identified as training or test accuracy in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in large convolutional networks, corrupted or random labels, CIFAR-100, and model-size or regularization effects.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima, and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation in batch-normalized convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; special convolutional initialization and Fixup.

Orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, orthogonal convolution kernels, 10,000-layer convolutional networks, and direct comparisons among standard activation-matched initialization schemes. Fixed-budget accuracy does not establish eventual convergence or equal asymptotic accuracy.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, catapult recovery, curvature trajectories, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
Batch normalization comparisons, learning-rate tolerance attributable to normalization, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Figure 7's off-critical comparison should be retained when correcting R7, so no additional missing row is required. Exact plotted accuracies are unavailable in the supplied text, but explicit qualitative descriptions establish the reported directions.

versions.untested_parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, and the effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima, and the effect of extra student neurons.
The paper studies fully connected networks without a plain-versus-residual comparison or batch normalization. It does not test whether identity shortcuts prevent depth-related training degradation.

The paper varies Gaussian weight and bias variances in tanh and SWISH networks, but does not compare activation-matched initialization schemes, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, or trainable depth in 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates above a stability limit, curvature or sharpness during training, and divergence thresholds.
Batch normalization versus no normalization, its effect on learning speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

rows.subject: tanh feedforward network
rows.operation_detail: Varied initial weight variance along the edge of chaos and measured MNIST accuracy at several learning rates.
rows.note: The text says accuracy drops beyond a point to the right of the line-of-uniformity and edge-of-chaos intersection; the drop-off location depends on learning rate.
rows.check: Critical initialization permits learning but does not ensure equal efficiency: accuracy after 30 epochs falls at larger variances, with a learning-rate-dependent threshold. Use lower-variance critical initializations as the comparison; accuracy is not explicitly identified as training or test accuracy.

rows.subject: tanh feedforward network
rows.size_stated: N = 784; depth swept up to L = 300
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; learning rate `10−3` for L < 100 and `10−4` for L ≥ 100
rows.operation_detail: Varied network depth at fixed initial weight and bias variances and measured MNIST learning accuracy.
rows.note: The text says learning remains efficient for very deep networks at the edge of chaos but eventually goes down at approximately L ∼ 270. The figure caption attributes the original finding to prior work, but this paper says it reproduces it.
rows.check: Figure 7 sweeps both depth and weight variance at fixed bias variance 0.05; weight variance 1.76 identifies its critical slice, not the entire experiment. Critical initialization allows efficient learning to much greater depth than off-critical initialization, with deterioration around depth 270. This is the authors' reproduction, not merely a cited result.

rows.subject: SWISH feedforward network
rows.stage_stated: trained on MNIST; initialization along the edge of chaos
rows.operation_detail: Varied initialization along the computable edge-of-chaos range and measured accuracy.

conditions.value: 21 equally-spaced points along the SWISH EOC

rows.note: The paper reports no significant accuracy differences across the computable range; a slightly lower learning rate was used for the left-most two points.
rows.check: Unchanged accuracy across an entirely critical SWISH range does not measure faster learning or greater trainable depth relative to another initialization. It cannot independently support V4. Learning rates also differ for the two leftmost points.

relationships.condition: 100-layer tanh networks initialized along the edge of chaos on MNIST and grayscale CIFAR-10
relationships.reason: R1–R4 show that criticality alone does not ensure equally fast learning: saturation at larger variances reduces fixed-budget accuracy, with the threshold depending on learning rate and dataset.
relationships.display_finding: Larger variances reduced accuracy within the training budget through saturation, with thresholds depending on learning rate and dataset.
